Naomi / team — quick responses and next steps from infra/runtime perspective:

1) Multiple IdPs: Redwood supports multiple SAML IdPs for a single customer. We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows; the main caveat is session affinity and default-redirect behavior when more than one IdP is present. For the merger window we recommend:
   - Primary IdP: use SP-initiated for day-to-day;
   - Secondary IdP: configure as fall-back with explicit relay-state rules.

2) SCIM: Our provisioning pipeline supports core RFC7643 attributes and a configurable transformer that can ingest custom attributes (boolean/string). We can map a contractor boolean into group membership via a small mapping rule (we'll provide examples). See attached scim_mapping_template.csv.

3) IP allowlist vs VPN: If Finova can provide stable egress IPs (even a small /28 or /27 range) we can add them to the tenant allowlist. If not feasible, private peering or a VPN tunnel is an acceptable alternative; VPN is easier for dynamic ranges but increases setup lead time. Recommend we treat the first 30 days as "staging" with relaxed CIDR and move to a tightened /28 at cutover.

4) Service accounts / token rotation: We support short-lived tokens and long-lived service API keys. We recommend the pattern: service-account-redwood-{customer}-{env} (e.g., service-account-redwood-finova-prod). For security we prefer short-lived tokens tied to your KMS; otherwise if you require long-lived keys we'll enforce automated rotation every 30 days and will log usages to the audit stream. Attached: service_account_pattern.md.

Next steps: I'll join the Tue 11/9 10:00 PT call. Action items before the call:
- Marissa: post the SCIM template and example mapping to the shared drive.
- Naomi: collect Finova's IP ranges or VPN preference and share with infra by EOD 11/6.
